claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-0:docs/team/sprint-example.md line 17: "| Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy | Dev 3 | 2 | Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau |". No line in the file gives a reason for the delay.

Lines 31-33: "Việc "Ngừng gửi thông báo" chưa xong nên không được trình diễn — chưa xong thì chưa tính, dù đã viết gần hết code." Consistent with Scrum Guide 2020: "If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review."

Lines 37-39: "Làm tốt: viết tiêu chí chấp nhận trước khi code…", "Cần sửa: nhận việc phụ thuộc vào một người duy nhất.", "Hành động cho sprint sau: mỗi việc lớn hơn 3 điểm phải có hai người đọc code." None mentions an estimate. Both quoted code blocks match the file character-for-character.

Round 2: section 4 now says the retrospective "is one place to talk about why an item took longer" and summary 4 says "for example at the retrospective" - no longer exclusive. Scrum Guide 2020: "The Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint." Comparing a guess with reality can only happen after the work; supportable as hedged opinion.

Round 3: section 4 now reads "People who are held to their guesses tend to start protecting themselves: they give bigger numbers next time ... or they call work \"done\" when it is not"; summary 3 "tends to push"; section 6 "the numbers tend to grow bigger". The hedge scopes the whole list; "Either way, the numbers stop describing the work" is conditional on those behaviours (inflated numbers by definition no longer describe the work). No Scrum Guide 2020 statement on this; supportable as hedged opinion consistent with why-estimate claim 6.
claim_verdicts.source: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html (checked; no statement on estimate inflation)

claim_verdicts.evidence: Scrum Guide 2020, Commitment: Definition of Done: "If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review. Instead, it returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration." Lesson's "is not presented at the Sprint Review and goes back to the Product Backlog for later" matches.

Scrum Guide 2020, Commitment: Sprint Goal: "For the Sprint Backlog it is the Sprint Goal." "Although the Sprint Goal is a commitment by the Developers, it provides flexibility in terms of the exact work needed to achieve it." Sprint Planning speaks of "Sprint forecasts"; the Guide nowhere makes an estimate or story point a commitment (fetched page shows no mention of story points).

git show stage-0:docs/team/sprint-example.md line 31: "Đội trình diễn trên môi trường thử nghiệm, không phải trên máy cá nhân." Lines 37-39 (retrospective) do not mention "Ngừng gửi thông báo" or any estimate; the action applies to "việc lớn hơn 3 điểm", so not the 2-point item.

Scrum Guide 2020, Sprint Retrospective: "The purpose of the Sprint Retrospective is to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness." "The Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint." Lesson: "the meeting at the end of the sprint where the team looks at how it worked" matches.

issues.text: q3 explanation d states as certain what the lesson now hedges (section 4: "planning tends to get worse"; claim 5). The other q3 explanations were fixed this round; this one was left unhedged.
issues.quote: Choosing numbers to look good stops them describing the work, so planning gets worse.
issues.fix: q3 explanation d en: "so planning gets worse" -> "so planning tends to get worse"; vi: "nên lập kế hoạch tệ đi" -> "nên lập kế hoạch thường tệ đi".

issues.text: The new sprint-goal paragraph sits between 'treats every estimate as a commitment' and 'That has a cost.' Reading in order, 'That' now seems to point at the sprint goal commitment, so I first read it as 'committing to the sprint goal has a cost' and had to re-read the previous two paragraphs.
issues.fix: Replace 'That has a cost.' with 'Treating estimates as promises has a cost.'

issues.text: Now I know the team commits to the sprint goal. My next question is not answered: when one item does not finish, did the team break its goal commitment? The lesson never says what Sprint 14's goal was or whether one unfinished item means the goal was missed, so 'not proof that someone broke a promise' feels half-supported.
issues.quote: the team commits to the goal, not to each item's number.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after 'they are not promises in themselves' saying whether a single unfinished item by itself means the sprint goal was missed (and, if the file states Sprint 14's goal, whether it was met).

issues.text: After 'This matches the Scrum Guide ... goes back to the Product Backlog', the phrase 'the team's own choice: the item moves to the next sprint' makes me stop: is moving to the next sprint a different thing from going back to the Product Backlog, and did the team go against the Guide? The text hints at a difference but does not say how the two fit.
issues.quote: Sprint 14's file records the team's own choice: the item moves to the next sprint.
issues.fix: Add half a sentence: going back to the Product Backlog means the item can be picked again later, and Sprint 14's team chose to pick it again in the next sprint.

issues.text: Carried from round 1: the situation still does not say which team or sprint this is. The 'tests are not finished' detail is not in Sprint 14's file, so in section 5 I am unsure whether it is the same item or a made-up one.
issues.quote: On the last day of a sprint, one item estimated at 2 points is still open.
issues.fix: Start with 'On the last day of a sprint like Sprint 14 in the Đơn Hàng team, ...' so the reader knows it is a similar, not identical, case.

issues.text: Carried from round 1: q4 distractors b, c, d still have nothing in the scenario pointing to them (no slowing, no hours, no meeting timing), so a is guessable without understanding. The explanations now say so openly, which confirms they were never serious options.
issues.quote: Items were marked done before they really were
issues.fix: Replace one distractor with a plausible one, e.g. 'The items were estimated too small, so they could not be finished properly'.

issues.text: q5: the key is a close paraphrase of 'The retrospective does not discuss the unfinished item at all', and b, c, d are easy to rule out by just scanning the three quoted lines, so the question tests recall of the file more than the idea.
issues.quote: It does not mention it; its lines are about how the team works
issues.fix: Make one distractor plausible, e.g. 'It adds an action that covers this item: two people read its code'.

skipped_steps: Team commits to the sprint goal -> unfinished item is not a broken promise: whether one unfinished item breaks the goal is not stated.
Guide: item goes back to the Product Backlog -> file: moved to next sprint: how the two relate is hinted, not said.
